about.label: about
about.lead: Hi! My name is Rodrigo Dutra.
about.body: Hi! My name is Rodrigo Dutra Ferreira. I'm a Software Engineering student at the University of Brasília (UnB), currently in my fifth semester, and part of CJR, UnB's computing junior enterprise, where I work on real projects for clients and learn firsthand how team development works.
about.body2: I'm passionate about technology and continuous learning; I believe getting a little better every day is the secret to becoming a good professional. My main focus is the Node.js and TypeScript ecosystem, and I've delivered several full-stack projects from start to finish, from the PostgreSQL data model to containerized deployment with Docker and CI/CD on GitHub Actions. I also have experience with agile methods (Scrum and XP), technical documentation, and multidisciplinary teamwork, plus I keep a homelab where I apply infrastructure and cloud concepts. Besides programming languages, I speak English and Italian fluently.

projects.label: projects
projects.intro: A selection of what I've built, from full stack to the terminal and infrastructure.

bookshelf.description: Full stack app to manage a personal library and track reading habits, with Google Books search and Gemini-powered recommendations.
bookshelf.overview: Bookshelf App is a full stack app to manage a personal library and track reading habits: catalog books, log progress, add ratings and notes, and see stats. I integrated the Google Books API for search and Google Gemini for personalized recommendations. It's built with Next.js, tRPC, Prisma, and PostgreSQL, with Auth.js, Docker, GitHub Actions, Vitest tests, and a Vercel deploy, aiming for practices close to production.

algocards.description: Flashcards for algorithms and data structures using FSRS-6 spaced repetition to schedule reviews and prep for technical interviews.
algocards.overview: AlgoCards is a flashcards platform for studying algorithms and data structures, focused on interview prep. It uses FSRS-6 spaced repetition to decide when each card is due, with support for code and complexity cards. I implemented and tested my own FSRS module with property-based tests and reference cases, on top of Next.js, tRPC, Prisma, and PostgreSQL.

stockio.description: Marketplace backend covering users, stores, products, and categories, built during the CJR trainee process, with JWT auth and password recovery.
stockio.overview: Stock.io is a marketplace backend I built during the CJR trainee process, covering users, stores, products, and categories. I implemented JWT authentication and email-based password recovery, practicing API structure, ORM, and environment variables. It was built with NestJS, TypeScript, Prisma, and PostgreSQL.

homelab.description: Self-hosted development environment on Fedora Linux, running services with Docker, a reverse proxy, monitoring, and reproducible backups.
homelab.overview: Dev Homelab is my personal environment for studying infrastructure, Docker, and DevOps. I turned a MacBook Air into a server on Fedora Linux, hosting PostgreSQL, Redis, Traefik, Portainer, Prometheus, Grafana, and Uptime Kuma. I practiced containerization, reverse proxy, TLS, Docker networks, monitoring, backups, and secret management, using Docker Compose and scripts to keep it reproducible.

piggyme.description: Personal finance app with income, expenses, goals, and dashboards, built as a team for the Software Development Methods course at UnB.
piggyme.overview: PiggyMe is a personal finance app built as a team (the Brooks team) for the Software Development Methods course at UnB. It handles income and expenses, financial goals, and tracking through dashboards and charts, with gamification elements. I worked with Node.js, Express, MySQL, and JavaScript, plus JWT, bcrypt, and Nodemailer.

unitask.description: Full stack task manager with auth, a calendar, and a weekly activity chart drawn with the Canvas API, no external libraries.
unitask.overview: UniTask is a full stack task manager built with a classmate. It lets you register and authenticate users, create tasks with dates, view them in a calendar, and see a weekly activity chart and a progress summary. I used JavaScript, Express, JWT, bcrypt, and Supabase, and drew the chart directly with the Canvas API, no external libraries.

budgetpro.description: Personal finance dashboard in vanilla JS: income, expenses, a chart, and live BRL/USD conversion via the Frankfurter API.
budgetpro.overview: BudgetPro is a personal finance dashboard in plain HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. You can add and delete income and expenses, track balance and totals, filter and sort transactions, view a chart, and convert BRL/USD in real time via the Frankfurter API. It consolidated fundamentals like the Fetch API, async/await, DOM manipulation, Chart.js, localStorage, CSV export, CSS Grid, and the BEM methodology.

atividadeDocker.description: CJR Docker track exercise: containerizing a message-board API with PostgreSQL, multi-stage images, Compose, and publishing to GHCR.
atividadeDocker.overview: Atividade Docker is part of CJR's Docker track and aims to containerize an app hands-on. Starting from a simple message-board API, I set up a PostgreSQL container, the API itself, and the communication between services. I practiced Dockerfiles, multi-stage images, Docker Compose, volumes, networks, and environment variables, and published images to GHCR with GitHub Actions.

learning.description: A running log of my studies and exercises through the year, from data structures and compilers to TypeScript, NestJS, and SQL.
learning.overview: Learning Journal 2026 is my log of studies, exercises, and projects through the year. It gathers data structures and algorithms, TypeScript, NestJS, Oracle SQL, object orientation, and compilers. The idea is to put the concepts I study in my degree into code and explore new tools, tracking my progress.
